About

Song Bio

“Never Gonna Give You Up” is known as the world famous Rick Roll song.

The music video, directed by Simon West, finds Astley singing at various west London locales, including an empty club where he gradually inspires a bartender (played by dancer Clive Clarke of the Top of the Pops dance troupe Zoo) to bust a move. Apparently, Clarke had been nursing a serious hangover when his attempt to do a stunt flip went awry, and he landed on his head. Luckily, he wasn’t injured and nailed the stunt on another take.

Rick had not originally wanted to create a music video for this song, but he was eventually forced to by the director.

Once the internet revived the song’s popularity, some realized Robo’s theme from the Super Nintendo game Chrono Trigger bore a striking resemblance to “Never Gonna GIve You Up”. It was a coincidence, as the game’s composer had never heard Rick Astley’s song. Still, mash-ups of both are common. The 1987 video was officially uploaded to YouTube on the 24th of October 2009 and has over one billion views as of 2021. Never Gonna Give You Up sheet music is also available for free.

Q&A

Find answers to frequently asked questions about the song and explore its deeper meaning

How did the Rick Roll came to be?
Genius Answer

4chan had a prank where links advertising for something instead linked to a picture of Duckroll (itself inspired by a word replacer that changed “egg” to “duck”, hence “eggroll” = “duckroll”). Then in 2007, as the Grand Theft Auto IV trailer was unavailable due to heavy traffic, someone on /v/ posted a link that actually led to “Never Gonna Give You Up” – evolving the “Duckroll” into the “Rickroll”. One year later, it had broken out of the Imageboards, to the point YouTube’s April Fools prank linked every video on the main page to “Never Gonna Give You Up” and Rick Astley partook in a Macy’s Thanksgiving parade rickroll.

–Source: KnowYourMeme

When was the original song recorded?
Genius Answer

Apparently it was recorded in 1987 at the PWL Studios in South London, and released July 27th that same year. (Source)

Was Rick Astley the original writer of this song?
Genius Answer

No, Never Gonna Give You Up was written by Mike Stock, Matt Aitken, and Pete Waterman, the famous trio of producers who brought considerable fame to a great many of the 1980’s biggest pop sensations.
